title: Hawaiian Maui and the Fishing Hook
subtitle: A chant of Kualii describes land drawn from the sea

learningObjectives.text: What does Maui pull from the sea?

chant.work: Legends of Ma-Ui, a Demi God of Polynesia and of his Mother Hina
chant.author: W. D. Westervelt
chant.locator: Chapter II · MAUI THE FISHERMAN; Chapter II · MAUI THE FISHERMAN, normalized characters 24-536
chant.excerpt: Oh the great fish hook of Maui! Manai-i-ka-lani 'Made fast to the heavens'--its name; An earth-twisted cord ties the hook. Engulfed from the lofty Kauiki. Its bait the red billed Alae, The bird made sacred to Hina. It sinks far down to Hawaii, Struggling and painfully dying. Caught is the land under the water, Floated up, up to the surface, But Hina hid a wing of the bird And broke the land under the water. Below, was the bait snatched away And eaten at once by the fishes, The Ulua of the deep muddy places.
chant.note: Verbatim prose from Westervelt's early twentieth-century English compilation. Retain the named island/version; this is not a direct transcription of one oral performance.

narrativeBlocks.title: The magic hook
narrativeBlocks.body: Maui's fishing hook is Manaiakalani — in some tellings made from his grandmother's jawbone, in others a gift of the gods. It is the Polynesian Excalibur: the tool that makes him more than a trickster.

narrativeBlocks.title: A fishing trip that moves the world
narrativeBlocks.body: He goes out with his brothers to fish — and hooks not a fish but the sea-floor itself: the chant of Kualii records him heaving until islands rise from the deep.

narrativeBlocks.title: The brothers' forbidden look
narrativeBlocks.body: Some versions say the brothers must not look back while he hauls; they look — the line slackens, the catch breaks apart, and the islands come up scattered instead of whole.

narrativeBlocks.title: The islands as bycatch
narrativeBlocks.body: Hawaii claims Maui fished up its islands; New Zealand claims its North Island is the great fish itself, Te Ika a Maui. The same feat explains different maps.

narrativeBlocks.title: A hero who fishes
narrativeBlocks.body: Where other myth-heroes slay monsters, Maui's signature feat is fishing — the ocean itself is his prey, and the land is the catch.

quiz.prompt: What does Maui pull from the sea with his hook?

choices.text: The largest fish in the world
The lost city of the gods
Islands — the sea-floor itself, hauled up as land

quiz.explanation: The catch is land — islands raised by a fishing line.

quiz.prompt: What do the brothers do that breaks the catch?

choices.text: They look back at the forbidden moment — the line slackens and the islands scatter
They cut the line in jealousy

quiz.explanation: The glance costs the whole catch — the taboo broken.
